messages.content: Provide a comprehensive analysis, including specific examples, of the advantages and disadvantages of online art classes compared to traditional in-person classes, and address factors such as technical requirements, level of interaction between students and instructors, the ability to receive feedback, the quality of materials used, and the effectiveness of the instructional methods employed.

Online art classes and traditional in-person classes both have their own set of advantages and disadvantages. An analysis of these factors can help students make informed decisions on which type of class to take, based on their personal preferences and requirements. 

Technical Requirements:

Advantages: Online art classes require a computer, internet access and a few software applications. This makes them accessible from virtually anywhere in the world, making it easier for students to participate no matter where they are situated.

Disadvantages: Online art classes may not be available to students who don’t have access to computers or reliable internet service. As technical difficulties are bound to happen, students may experience connectivity issues during the class or disruption in the streaming of Lecture videos that may lead to missing out on lessons.

Level of Interaction between Students and Instructors:

Advantages: Online art classes provide more flexibility in terms of schedule as well as instructors from different locations or countries. The chat and messaging options available on the platform allow students to ask questions and receive responses quickly, offering seamless interactions with instructors despite the distance.

Disadvantages: Traditional art classes generally have more engagement between the instructor and the student. This is due to the nature of seeing and receiving feedback on the physical work, which cannot be perceived with the same level of accuracy through webcam or screen. Realtime communication with group/team is also not as feasible on online classes, making it difficult for students to build relationships with other art enthusiasts in the class.

The Ability to Receive Feedback:

Advantages: Online art classes provide immediate feedback from instructors, because they are not bound by time and location restrictions. Instead of an immediate response, students can save important assignment questions or work and respond later once they have given it due thought.

Disadvantages: Traditional art classes provide feedback soon after the completion or submitting work. The face-to-face interaction between the student and the teacher provides the opportunity for immediate and detailed feedback, which is not always possible with online art classes.

The Quality of Materials Used:

Advantages: Online art classes often provide students with a wide range of materials to choose from, including more modern digital tools and software, and new techniques can be introduced which are not readily available in traditional classes. This gives students the freedom to explore and experiment with a myriad of art styles, mediums and materials based on personal interest and individual preferences.

Disadvantages: Traditional art classes offer students the chance to work with physical materials with the instructor's guidance to help them understand how to manipulate and use them effectively. Replicating these hands-on techniques with online materials may not be as easy, and may require additional practice outside of class time which may not always be possible.

Effectiveness of Instructional Methods Employed:

Advantages: Online art classes use tools such as online lectures, recorded videos of demonstrations, diagrams and drawings which can be paused, listened to over and over again, and rewound for more effective absorption of the knowledge imparted.

Disadvantages: Traditional art classes are often more designed for experiential learning, which is ideal for those who like to learn by doing. It is less challenging to relate to concepts such as color theory if given the chance to engage in a practical situation with instructor guidance.

Conclusion:

In conclusion, online art classes offer flexibility in terms of scheduling and location, with access to a wide variety of materials and instructional support. Traditional art classes provide an immediate interaction among students and instructors, a chance for hands-on training of physical materials and more practical application of techniques. Ultimately, personal preference, location, finances and other factors will help determine which type of art class is best suited to the student's needs.

The guide should also highlight any alternative ingredients that can be used to adjust the flavor or consistency of the dip, and provide nutritional information for those following a particular diet. Creamy Vegan Spinach and Artichoke Dip Recipe

Looking for a delicious, plant-based dip to serve at your next party or get-together? Look no further than this vegan spinach and artichoke dip! It's easy to make, packed with flavor, and perfect for dipping crackers, chips, or veggies.

Ingredients:

- 1 14-ounce can of artichoke hearts, drained and chopped
- 1 10-ounce package of frozen spinach, thawed and drained
- 1 cup of vegan cream cheese
- 1/2 cup of vegan sour cream
- 1/2 cup of vegan mayo
- 1/2 cup of nutritional yeast
- 1/4 cup of diced onion
- 3 cloves of garlic, minced
- 1/4 teaspoon of salt
- 1/4 teaspoon of black pepper

Instructions:

1. Preheat your oven to 375 degrees Fahrenheit.

2. In a large bowl, combine the artichoke hearts, spinach, vegan cream cheese, vegan sour cream, vegan mayo, nutritional yeast, onion, garlic, salt, and black pepper. Stir everything together until it's well combined.

3. Pour the mixture into a 9-inch baking dish, and smooth it out into an even layer.

4. Bake the dip for 25-30 minutes, or until it's hot and bubbly and the top is lightly browned.

5. Remove the dip from the oven, and let it cool for a few minutes before serving.

6. To serve the dip, set out crackers, chips, or veggies for dipping. You can also sprinkle a little extra nutritional yeast or chopped fresh herbs on top of the dip for added flavor.

Cooking Tips:

- For a stronger garlic flavor, try adding an extra clove of minced garlic to the dip.
- If you prefer a thinner dip, you can stir in a little almond milk or vegetable broth to thin it out to your desired consistency.
- Don't have nutritional yeast? Try using a little extra vegan cream cheese or vegan mayo instead, or make your own vegan Parmesan cheese by blending together 1/2 cup of raw cashews, 1/2 cup of nutritional yeast, and 1/2 teaspoon of salt.
- Want to make the dip ahead of time? You can assemble it up to a day in advance, then cover it and refrigerate it until you're ready to bake it. Just add an extra 10-15 minutes to the baking time if it's cold when you put it in the oven.

Serving and Storing Suggestions:

- Serve the dip warm, straight out of the oven, or let it cool to room temperature if you prefer.
- Leftovers can be stored in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3-4 days. Reheat the dip in the oven or microwave before serving.
- This dip also freezes well. Transfer it to a freezer-safe container or zipper bag, and freeze for up to 2 months. Thaw the dip in the refrigerator overnight before reheating it.

Nutritional Information:

This vegan spinach and artichoke dip is packed with protein, fiber, and healthy fats. Here's a breakdown of the nutritional information for one serving (assuming 8 servings per recipe):

Describe the steps one must follow to create a sustainable fitness routine that can be maintained over a long period of time without burning out or losing motivation. Include details on selecting suitable exercises, setting achievable goals, incorporating rest and recovery, staying accountable, and adjusting the routine as needed.

1. Determine your fitness goals: Before starting a fitness routine, it is essential to have clear goals in mind. This will help you stay motivated and focused on your workouts. Whether your goal is to lose weight, build muscle, or improve your cardiovascular health, you need to have a specific target to work towards.

2. Choose exercises that suit your fitness level: The key to building a sustainable workout routine is to choose exercises that are achievable and effective. You should select exercises that are suitable for your fitness level and that you enjoy doing.

3. Plan a workout schedule: Once you have chosen the exercises, you need to plan your workout schedule. Determine the number of days a week you will be working out and for how long. This will help you establish a routine and stay consistent.

4. Incorporate rest and recovery: Rest and recovery are crucial for a sustainable workout routine. You must give your body time to rest and recover between workouts. Incorporate recovery days into your routine to give your muscles time to heal.

5. Stay accountable: Staying accountable is critical to ensure that you stick to your fitness routine. You can enlist the help of a workout partner, hire a personal trainer, or join a fitness group to hold you accountable.

6. Adjust your routine as needed: As your fitness level improves, you will need to adjust your routine to continue to challenge your body. Change your exercises, increase the intensity or frequency of your workouts, or set new goals to keep you motivated and engaged.

7. Reward yourself: Rewarding yourself for achieving your fitness goals is a great way to stay motivated. Celebrate your successes, no matter how small, and use them as fuel to keep pushing towards your goals.

In conclusion, creating a sustainable fitness routine requires discipline, dedication, and planning. By choosing the right exercises, setting achievable goals, incorporating rest and recovery, staying accountable, and adjusting your routine as needed, you can build a sustainable fitness routine that will help you achieve your fitness goals and improve your overall health and wellbeing.

Analyze the specific ways in which the architecture of ancient Greek temples influenced the content, style, and overall design of modern Greek buildings, and provide examples that highlight these connections. Additionally, consider the cultural and societal factors that shaped the evolution of these architectural influences, and how they are represented in contemporary Greek architecture.

The architecture of ancient Greek temples had a significant influence on the content, style, and overall design of modern Greek buildings. The principles of ancient Greek architecture, including balance, symmetry, proportion, and harmony, are fundamental elements of modern Greek architecture. These elements continue to be used in contemporary Greek architecture as they provide a timeless design language that reflects the ancient Greek origins.

One of the most noticeable connections between ancient Greek and modern Greek architecture is the use of columns. The Greeks used columns to support their buildings while also giving them a grand and impressive appearance. These columns were typically characterized by their fluted shafts and decorative capitals, which gave them a distinct Greek style. Modern Greek architects have continued this tradition by incorporating columns into their designs. For example, one of the most famous modern Greek buildings that use columns is the Athens Academy, which was designed in the neoclassical style.

Another connection between ancient Greek and modern Greek architecture is the use of marble. The Greeks were masters at working with marble, and they used it extensively in their buildings. Marble was not only durable, but it gave their buildings a regal appearance. Modern Greek architects have continued this tradition, and marble is still a common material used in contemporary Greek architecture. The Acropolis Museum in Athens is a prime example of a modern Greek building that utilizes marble extensively.

The cultural and societal factors that shaped the evolution of these architectural influences are rooted in the importance that the Greeks placed on art, beauty, and perfection. The Greeks believed that architecture was an art form that should embody these ideals. They also believed that buildings should be in harmony with their surroundings and should reflect the values and culture of their society. These cultural beliefs continue to influence modern Greek architecture as architects seek to create designs that are beautiful, functional, and in harmony with their environment.

In conclusion, the architecture of ancient Greek temples has had a significant influence on modern Greek architecture. The use of elements such as columns and marble, as well as the principles of balance, proportion, and harmony, are fundamental elements of contemporary Greek architecture. These architectural influences are rooted in the cultural and societal beliefs of the Greeks, which continue to influence Greek architecture today.

The Importance of Communication Skills in Conflict Avoidance

Communication is an integral part of our daily lives. Whether it is verbal or nonverbal, we are constantly communicating with those around us. However, effective communication goes beyond just talking and listening. It involves understanding, empathy, and the ability to convey messages clearly and concisely. In this article, we will explore the importance of communication skills in conflict avoidance and provide practical tips for improving communication skills to prevent misunderstandings and tensions.

Effective communication in personal relationships

Miscommunication often leads to conflicts in personal relationships. For instance, when one partner fails to express their needs and desires clearly, it may lead to misunderstandings, arguments, and resentment. On the other hand, effective communication helps partners to avoid misunderstandings, build trust, and deepen their bond. Effective communication strategies in personal relationships include:

Active listening: This strategy involves focusing on the speaker and giving them your undivided attention. By actively listening, we hear the speaker's tone, emotions, and body language, which helps us to understand their message.

Avoiding assumptions: Assumptions often fuel conflicts in relationships. Instead of assuming what the other person is thinking or feeling, ask for clarification. This way, you can avoid misunderstandings and clear up any confusion.

Using "I" statements: "I" statements express your feelings and opinions without blaming or attacking the other person. This strategy helps to avoid defensiveness and encourages open communication and problem-solving.

Effective communication in the workplace

Communication is essential in the workplace, where different people with different personalities, backgrounds, and opinions work together to achieve a common goal. Ineffective communication leads to misunderstandings, decreased productivity, and conflict. To avoid these pitfalls, the following communication strategies are useful:

Clear communication: Communication should be clear and concise, avoiding jargon or technical terms that may be difficult for some to understand.

Active listening: In the workplace, active listening can help colleagues to understand one another better and avoid misunderstandings.

Choosing the right medium: Different communication channels, such as email, phone calls, or face-to-face conversations, are suitable for different types of messages. Choosing the right one improves clarity and comprehension.

Nonverbal communication: Facial expressions, gestures, and posture convey messages in the workplace. Paying attention to these nonverbal cues helps to prevent misunderstandings and resolve conflicts.

Effective communication in group settings

Communication in group settings, such as in meetings, can be tricky. However, good communication skills can help prevent conflicts and promote productivity. Here are some tips for effective communication in group settings:

Clear agendas: When holding meetings, a clear agenda should be set to avoid confusion and keep the discussion on track.

Equal participation: Encourage everyone in the group to participate and listen to everyone's ideas before deciding on a course of action.

Nonverbal communication: Pay attention to nonverbal cues, such as body language and tone of voice. These can help to avoid misunderstandings and resolve conflicts.

Tips for improving communication skills in conflict resolution

Good communication is essential to resolving conflicts effectively. Here are some tips for improving communication skills in conflict resolution:

Be assertive: Being assertive involves standing up for yourself without attacking or blaming others. This approach helps to avoid defensiveness and promotes open communication.

Use "I" statements: "I" statements help to express your feelings and opinions without attacking or blaming others. This strategy encourages open communication and problem-solving.

Listen actively: Active listening helps you to focus on what the other person is saying, avoid misunderstandings, and show empathy.

Ask for clarification: When in doubt, ask for clarification. This approach can help you avoid misunderstandings and clear up any confusion.

Conclusion

Effective communication is essential in avoiding conflicts in various settings. Understanding how to communicate effectively is critical to prevent misunderstandings, promote productivity, deepen relationships, enhance collaboration, and resolve conflicts smoothly. By using clear communication, active listening, nonverbal communication, and other effective communication strategies, you can avoid misunderstandings, foster healthy relationships, and resolve conflicts calmly and constructively. Improving communication skills in conflict resolution takes practice, but by implementing the tips outlined in this article, you can become a more effective communicator in all areas of your life.

Title: DIY Macrame Plant Hanger

Introduction:
Macrame is an art form that involves knotting cords or strings into decorative or functional items. It is a popular technique used to create plant hangers, which are perfect for indoor or outdoor spaces. In this tutorial, we will be making a simple macrame plant hanger that can hold a small potted plant. This project is easy to follow, and you will need only a few tools and supplies.

What You Will Need:
- 3mm cotton cord (5 meters)
- Scissors
- Tape
- A small pot with a plant
- A measuring tape

Step 1: Cut the Cotton Cord
Cut the cotton cord into four equal lengths of 1.25 meters each. Tape the ends of the cords to prevent them from unraveling.

Step 2: Knot the Cords Together
Take the four cords and fold them in half. Make a knot at the top, leaving a loop large enough to hang the plant hanger. The loop should be approximately 13 inches from the top of the cords.

Step 3: Start the Macrame Knots
Divide the cords into groups of two, and knot them together 4 inches from the top knot. Use a half hitch knot by taking the right cord and placing it over the left cord. Take the right cord under the left cord and through the loop. Pull both cords to create a knot. Repeat the knot with the same cords, but this time, take the left cord over the right cord to complete the second half of the half hitch knot. Repeat the steps with the other set of cords.

Step 4: Add the Pot Holder
Place the pot on the cords to measure how far down you would like the hanger to be. Knot the cords together at that length using a square knot. To make the square knot, take the left cord and place it over the right cord. Take the right cord and place it over the left cord. Take the right cord under the left cord, and through the loop. Pull both cords to create the first half of the knot. Take the left cord and place it over the right cord. Take the left cord and place it under the right cord and through the loop. Pull both cords to complete the square knot.

Step 5: Add More Knots
Repeat step 3 by making half hitch knots with the cords. Continue knotting until it is 4 inches above the bottom knot to create a diamond-shaped pattern. Knot all the cords together at this point, leaving a loop large enough for the pot to sit in.

Step 6: Finish the Macrame Knots
Take all the cords and knot them together about 2 inches from the bottom knot, using a square knot.

Step 7: Trim the Ends
Trim the ends of the cords and unravel the ends to create a fringed look. You can also trim the ends to the same length to create a neat finish.

Your plant hanger is now complete! Hang it from the loop and place your potted plant in the pot holder.

Helpful Tips:
- Use a comb to unravel the ends more easily.
- Make the pot holder long enough to ensure that the pot fits securely.
- Use different colored cords to create a unique look.

- 10 drops essential oil (optional, for fragrance)

Necessary Tools:

- Measuring cups and spoons

Making homemade bread is a rewarding and delicious experience. The aroma of freshly baked bread wafting through the house is a sensory delight that can make anyone's mouth water. Here's how to make homemade bread:

Ingredients:
- 500g all-purpose flour
- 10g salt
- 7g instant yeast
- 350ml lukewarm water
- 1 tablespoon olive oil (optional)

Equipment:
- Mixing bowl
- Wooden spoon or stand mixer with dough-hook attachment
- Measuring cups and spoons
- Kitchen scale
- Plastic wrap or clean tea towel
- Bread loaf pan (optional)

Step 1: Mix the Dough
In a large mixing bowl, combine the flour, salt, and instant yeast. Mix until the ingredients are evenly distributed. Next, slowly add the lukewarm water, stirring with a wooden spoon or the dough hook attachment of your stand mixer until a shaggy dough forms. The dough should be slightly sticky, but if it's too wet, add a little more flour. If it's too dry, add a little water. Knead the dough for 5-10 minutes until it becomes smooth and elastic. If you're using a stand mixer, this process will only take about 5 minutes.

Step 2: Let the Dough Rise
Place the dough in a greased bowl (you can use olive oil to grease the bowl) and cover it with plastic wrap or a clean tea towel. Let the dough rise in a warm, draft-free place for 1-2 hours or until it has doubled in size. If your kitchen is chilly, you can heat the oven to the lowest possible temperature, then turn it off and use it as a warm, draft-free place for your dough to rise.

Step 3: Shape the Dough
After the dough has risen, gently punch it down and shape it into a ball. If you're using a bread loaf pan, lightly grease it with olive oil or non-stick spray and place the dough in the pan. If you prefer a free-form loaf, shape the dough into a round or oblong loaf and place it on a parchment-lined baking sheet. Cover the dough with plastic wrap or a clean tea towel and let it rise for another 30 minutes to 1 hour.

Step 4: Bake the Bread
Preheat your oven to 425 degrees Fahrenheit (218 degrees Celsius). If you're using a bread loaf pan, place it in the oven and bake for 30-35 minutes, or until the crust is golden brown and the bread sounds hollow when tapped on the bottom. If you're baking a free-form loaf, place it on a baking stone or a baking sheet, and bake for 25-30 minutes, or until the crust is golden brown and the bread sounds hollow when tapped on the bottom. Remove the bread from the oven and let it cool on a wire rack for at least 30 minutes before slicing and serving.

What was the impact of the Great Wall of China on the Silk Road trade route throughout history?

The Great Wall of China had a significant impact on the Silk Road trade route throughout history. 

During the Han Dynasty, the Great Wall was constructed to protect China from invading forces from the north, particularly the Xiongnu. The presence of the Great Wall created a physical barrier between China and the Central Asian trading partners on the Silk Road, making it difficult for trade to occur. As a result, the Silk Road trade route bypassed the Great Wall by going through the Hexi Corridor, a narrow passage between the Great Wall and the Qilian Mountains. This route allowed the trade to continue between China and Central Asia.

During the Tang Dynasty, the Great Wall no longer served as a military defense, and China's rulers opened up trade with Central Asia. The Tang emperors extended the Great Wall, sometimes diverting the Silk Road, to protect trade caravans from banditry. During this time, Chinese goods such as silk and porcelain were in high demand among the Central Asian people, and demand for Central Asian products such as horses and jade increased in China.

After the Yuan Dynasty, the importance of the Silk Road trade route diminished as the maritime trade route became more profitable. The Great Wall was no longer a significant factor in the Silk Road trade route. However, the Great Wall remains a popular tourist attraction and a symbol of Chinese ingenuity and strength.

#!/bin/bash

# This script takes two arguments as input: the path of a directory and a number of days (X)
# It searches recursively for all files that were modified X or more days ago in that directory and its subdirectories
# The script then deletes all the discovered files without prompting for confirmation

# Check that two arguments have been provided
if [ $# -lt 2 ]; then
   echo "ERROR: Two arguments are required: directory path and number of days"
   exit 1
fi

# Get the directory path and number of days from the input arguments
dir_path=$1
num_days=$2

# Check that the provided directory path is valid
if [ ! -d "$dir_path" ]; then
   echo "ERROR: Invalid directory path"
   exit 1
fi

# Check that the provided number of days is a valid integer
re='^[0-9]+$'
if ! [[ $num_days =~ $re ]]; then
   echo "ERROR: Number of days must be a valid integer"
   exit 1
fi

echo "Searching for files in $dir_path modified $num_days or more days ago..."

# Find all files in the directory and its subdirectories that were modified X or more days ago
find "$dir_path" -type f -mtime +"$num_days" -print0 | while read -d $'\0' file
do
   echo "Deleting file: $file"

done

echo "Finished deleting files modified $num_days or more days ago in $dir_path and its subdirectories"

One of my favorite dishes that I tried while traveling through Thailand is called Massaman Curry. It's a mild and creamy curry dish that is loaded with flavorful spices and tender chunks of meat.

Ingredients:
- 1 lb of beef or chicken cut into small bite-sized pieces
- 1 can of coconut milk
- 1-2 tablespoons of Massaman curry paste
- 1 onion, roughly chopped
- 2-3 potatoes, cut into small pieces
- 1 carrot, peeled and chopped
- 1 tablespoon of tamarind paste
- 1 tablespoon of palm sugar
- 1 tablespoon of fish sauce
- 1 cinnamon stick
- 3-4 cardamom pods
- 3-4 cloves
- 1-2 bay leaves
- 1 cup of chicken or beef broth
- 1-2 tablespoons of roasted peanuts
- a handful of fresh cilantro leaves

Directions:
1. Begin by heating a large pot or dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add the curry paste and whisk it for about 1 minute.

2. Next, add the onions and sauté until they become translucent. Then add the meat and cook until browned on all sides.

3. Add the potatoes, carrots, cinnamon, cardamom, cloves, and bay leaves. Stir to combine everything and sauté for about 1-2 minutes.

4. In a separate bowl, combine the coconut milk, tamarind paste, palm sugar, and fish sauce, and mix until combined. Then pour it into the pot.

5. Add chicken or beef broth to the pot, bringing it to a simmer. Cover and let everything cook for approximately 30 minutes, or until the meat and potatoes are tender.

6. Once the curry has finished cooking, remove the cinnamon stick, bay leaves, and any cardamom pods. Be sure to taste the curry and adjust the seasoning (salt, tamarind or sugar) if needed.

7. To serve, spoon the curry into bowls, and sprinkle roasted peanuts and cilantro on top. For the best dining experience, serve with white rice.

Special cooking techniques: For more authentic flavors, you can roast the spices, peanuts, and chilies in a dry skillet before adding them to the curry. Additionally, you can add thinly sliced shallots and roasted potatoes to garnish the curry before serving. 

Presentation suggestions: Thai food is all about presentation! So, you can transfer your curry to a serving dish and surround it with bowls of white rice, pickled vegetables, and fresh herbs to create a colorful and visually appealing table.

They exhibit unique physical properties, such as the Meissner effect, wherein they exclude magnetic fields from their interiors, and persistent currents, which continue to flow indefinitely in superconducting loops. Interesting applications of superconductors include the following:

1. Superconducting magnets: Superconducting materials are widely used to make powerful magnets for scientific research, medical applications such as Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI), and particle accelerators such as the Large Hadron Collider.

2. Power transmission: Superconducting cables can transmit electricity more efficiently than traditional copper cables. They are currently being tested for use in power grids.

3. Energy storage: Superconducting coils can store a significant amount of energy, making them suitable for use in energy storage systems.

4. Transportation: Superconducting levitation systems, such as Maglev trains, use magnetic repulsion to levitate and propel trains at high speeds.

5. Computing: Superconducting materials are used to make qubits, the building blocks of quantum computers.

6. Sensing: Superconducting sensors offer high sensitivity and resolution for detecting magnetic fields, radiation, and temperature changes, among other things.

In conclusion, superconductors have a wide range of potential applications, particularly in power transmission, transportation, computing, and sensing. As our understanding of these materials improves, it is likely that new applications will emerge in the future.

Given the text: Lately I’ve been using a lot of Reactjs goodness in my side projects. React is only the V in a modern day MVW (Model, View Whatever) pattern and that’s an interesting subject. Facebook uses its own Flux library/pattern/architecture to cope with the other stuff, however there seem to be a lot of different opinions when it’s comes to flux.
One of those flux variants is Redux, created by Dan Abramov and others. If you never heard of Redux or don’t really know how it works, I suggest you watch these videos first. In this blogpost I’ll explain a way of dealing with async operations using Redux Thunk.
The main reason why we can’t use async is due to the way a reducer function works. The concept of a reducer is that it takes the current state and an action and it returns the next state. It’s a pure function that does not modify the current state.
If would we want to do some async stuff we would have to wait until a Promise is resolved and then return the next state. We could just return the previous state and dispatch a new action once our Promise is resolved.
This is a bad approach because we can have side effects here.
The function is no longer pure. What if the Promise is rejected?
It’s also not allowed by the Redux store if you look at the source code.
Middleware is magical concept created by ancient elves riding unicorns. No not really, although I have to admit that it does seem a bit overwhelming at first. The essence of middleware is that it runs in the Store before the action is dispatched to the reducer. You can read the docs for the long version.
It provides a third-party extension point between dispatching an action, and the moment it reaches the reducer.
So basically the Thunk middleware stops the chain when the action is a function.
In the source of Thunk, the outcome of the action function gets returned but the value is most likely to be a Promise so I don’t think that it is necessary to return the value of action(store.dispatch, store.getState).
Enough with the theory, let’s create an actual example.
We’ll create a little app that fetches github repositories from a user.
When creating a Redux application I always find it helpful to have an idea of the application state. We need to store the username, the repositories and a flag whether we are loading the repos or not.
The first three action creators are easy to understand, they return an action, the end. As we saw in the code of Thunk the action can also be a function.
So our action creator that eventually does some async code should return a function.
Wait, wait, wait. An action creator that returns a function??!? How is that even an action creator? Well it isn’t really but it isn’t a reducer either, it’s a function that returns a function. So instead of debating on semantics let’s look at the code.
So the clue with the loadReposAction function is that we can do async stuff and then dispatch when we have something. Each dispatch call will run synchronously and update the application state. Whether we return the Promise of the fetch function doesn’t really matter.
So in order to bootstrap the application we’ll have to dispatch some actions to get things going.
To Thunk or not to Thunk?
So using the Thunk middleware we can execute async stuff. We briefly saw how middleware works and we most likely scratched our heads. Couldn’t we just call the loadReposAction directly and pass down the store?
Well turns out we can and none of this was really necessary. It seems like a good idea to keep the flow consistent and use the dispatcher for all actions. In the end it’s personal choice I think.
I’ve created a jsfiddle with the result.
Writing this blogpost really taught me how to use Redux Thunk, once you get it, it’s actually quite easy.
Middleware on the other hand can still be a bit confusing from time to time.
Please correct me if you find any mistakes.
I hope you enjoyed this blogpost and it all makes sense. If you have any suggestions or questions please leave a comment.

How do architects go about optimizing a building's orientation and overall site design to maximize its energy efficiency?

Architects go about optimizing a building's orientation and overall site design to maximize its energy efficiency by considering the following:

1. Solar orientation: The orientation of a building should maximize the amount of natural light and heat it receives from the sun, while minimizing the amount of solar gain during the summer months.

2. Building shape: The shape of the building should be designed to minimize surface area and thermal bridging, which can lead to significant heat loss or gain.

3. Site analysis: Architects should analyze the site before design to determine the prevailing wind patterns, natural and artificial shading, and solar access.

4. Passive solar design: This technique involves designing a building to take advantage of the sun’s natural energy for heating and cooling needs.

5. Thermal mass: The use of materials with high thermal mass, such as concrete or stone, can help regulate internal temperatures by absorbing and releasing heat.

6. Landscaping: A well-designed landscape can reduce the heat island effect, provide shade, and decrease water runoff.

7. Building envelope: A well-insulated building envelope can help reduce heating and cooling costs by minimizing air exchange between the interior and exterior of the building.

By considering these design elements, architects can create buildings that are optimized for energy efficiency and contribute to a more sustainable built environment.

Beef and Noodle Stir-fry Recipe

Ingredients:

1 pound beef sirloin or flank steak, sliced thinly against the grain

1 teaspoon salt

1/2 teaspoon black pepper

2 tablespoons olive oil

4 cloves garlic, minced

1 tablespoon grated ginger

1 large onion, sliced

1 bell pepper, sliced

1 cup beef broth

1 tablespoon soy sauce

1 tablespoon hoisin sauce

1 tablespoon cornstarch

1/4 cup water

8 ounces dried rice noodles

2 green onions, sliced

Cooking Tools:

Cutting board

Sharp knife

Large bowl

Large skillet

Spoon or spatula

Small bowl

Pot

Tongs

Instructions:

Step 1: Prepare the beef

Cut the beef into thin slices against the grain. Season with salt and pepper.

Step 2: Cook the noodles

Fill a pot with water and bring it to a boil. Add the rice noodles and cook for 4-5 minutes until tender. Drain and rinse with cold water.

Step 3: Prepare the vegetables

Cut the onion and bell pepper into thin slices. Mince the garlic and grate the ginger.

Step 4: Cook the beef

Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the beef slices and cook for 1-2 minutes on each side until browned. Remove from the skillet and set aside.

Step 5: Saute the vegetables

In the same skillet, add garlic, ginger, onion, and bell pepper. Saute for 2-3 minutes or until the vegetables are tender.

Step 6: Add broth and sauces

Add the beef broth, soy sauce, and hoisin sauce to the skillet. Stir to combine the ingredients.

Step 7: Thicken sauce

In a small bowl, mix the cornstarch and water until well combined. Add the mixture to the skillet and stir until the sauce thickens.

Step 8: Add the cooked beef and noodles

Add the cooked beef and rice noodles to the skillet. Toss everything to combine and cook for another 1-2 minutes until heated through.

Step 9: Serve

Serve the beef and noodle stir-fry while still hot. Garnish with green onions, if desired.

Difficulty level: Easy

Cooking time: Approximately 30 minutes

Variations and Substitutions:

Given the text: Auto industry exec turns to running as stress relief, inspiration. Mike Silvio speaks in Royal Oak on Oct. 11.
Mike Silvio of Livonia felt crushed by stress and anxiety and wondered how to channel the negative energy that disrupted his life at age 43 — as he watched his employer go through bankruptcy when the auto industry crashed during the Great Recession.
Now, a decade later, he is a marathon runner having not just competed on mountains, in deserts and across snow-covered vistas on every continent on Earth, but spending weekends and weeknights guiding others to find the drive to realize their dreams — whatever they may be.
“You spend your first 50 years building a resume, and the remainder of your life writing your eulogy,” said Silvio, whose professional life remains in the auto industry, leading a logistics tracking company.
But at 7 p.m. Thursday at the Royal Oak Public Library, the husband and father of two teenagers will share life lessons about the nonprofessional passion that changed his life — lessons learned while running about health, family, gratitude and perseverance, despite diabetes and heart issues.
In coming days, thousands of runners descend on the city for the Detroit Free Press/Chemical Bank Marathon, scheduled for Oct. 21. The marathon, which crosses into Canada, is part of three days of activities starting Oct. 19 and including a health and fitness expo, 5K and one-mile runs; a kids run and a half-marathon that stays on the U.S. Side of the border.
“There aren't many runners who will run at a slower pace to keep you from being alone for 13-plus miles. Michael is the guy who will run with you and wait for you,” said Kristin Meekhof, 44, an author and life coach from Royal Oak.
“During a half-marathon, I was really struggling," she said. "I told Michael to run ahead and he refused. He is the guy who waits to not only make sure that you cross the finish line but will run beside you to get you to it.
“I had a ton of self-doubt about training for the New York City Marathon. While running, I would say, ‘I don't know if I can do it.’ And he would say, ‘You're doing it. You're running now.’"
Not bad for a guy who has had two angioplasties and a stent in his chest.
Silvio runs in the pouring rain with beginners who lack confidence.
Today, Silvio is vice president of operations and innovation at Surgere — a "supply chain visibility" company that works with auto companies to track assets.
"A customer calls and says we want to track our parts and containers from start to finish," Silvio explains. "We can track the chain of custody and the timing. For example, a car company orders a widget, and we can say when it leaves the supplier, when the truck arrives at the border, when it gets to the plant and then how the empty containers get back to the supplier."
On top of everything else, he teaches at the Mike Ilitch School of Business at Wayne State University.
People know him from Berlin to New York for his 26.2-mile runs and inspirational speeches.
Silvio runs in the frigid Michigan winter, which he said can be colder than an Antarctic summer.
“He would be out at Kensington (Metropark) doing 20-mile training runs while most of us would run 8 miles and then go to breakfast,” said Al Johnson, 58, a retired Chrysler IT specialist from Plymouth.
Silvio and Suzi Stock, 58, a longtime running coach from Commerce Township, have prepared for marathons in minus 14 degrees, excluding wind chill.
“Isn’t that crazy?” Stock said. “We're out there thinking, should we be doing this? We should’ve just quit. We didn’t. He said, ‘Let’s go another half mile and see if our feet warm up.’ We ended up putting in 8 miles that day."
Guys like Silvio make the auto industry hum, friends and colleagues said.
Calvillo credits Silvio with his getting a promotion at work.
"He called me in, kicked the sales guy out, and said, ‘It’s going to be you and me. Together we’re going to put together numbers, proposals and figure it all out. If you make it work, you’re going to be a hero,” Calvillo recalled.
The two men worked to put logistics centers along border crossings in El Paso and Laredo, Texas.
Silvio says his running makes him focus at work. Colleagues say pressure is intense.
Brian Hagan, 47, of Brighton, a parts control team manager for Ford at the Chicago Assembly Plant, said Silvio — who works with multiple automakers — can lose tens of thousands of dollars if a plant shuts down for an unscheduled minute.
Silvio, a former rockabilly guitarist, notes that his grandfather came to Detroit from Italy.
"I have run many races in North America, but Detroit is my hometown race," Silvio said, though he is running a different marathon this month. "From the Ambassador Bridge, you see the sun rising over the Renaissance Center and return to the United States by the Windsor Tunnel. The world’s only underwater mile."
He has now run marathons on all seven continents — North America, South America, Europe, Africa, Asia, Australia and Antarctica.
"You could say my mission is now change," Silvio said, "to encourage others, mentor students, and continue to push myself so I can be here to share these life lessons and make a difference."
